bib.title: Cascaded Diffusion Models for High Fidelity Image Generation

question: Can a pipeline of diffusion models at increasing resolution, with no classifier guidance, reach state-of-the-art class-conditional ImageNet sample quality?
hypothesis: Augmenting the low-resolution conditioning input of super-resolution models alleviates compounding error from train-test mismatch and makes cascading beat non-cascaded models.
contributions: CDM yields samples superior to BigGAN-deep and VQ-VAE-2 in FID and CAS without any classifier
Conditioning augmentation (Gaussian noise for low-res upsampling, Gaussian blur for high-res) is critical; amortized training over augmentation strength enables post-training search

method.summary: Class-conditional pipeline of a 32x32 base diffusion model, a 32->64 super-resolution model, then 64->128 or 64->256 super-resolution models, each a separately trained U-Net. Super-resolution models are trained with conditioning augmentation (noise level s as extra embedding, or blur).
method.task: class-conditional ImageNet image generation (also unconditional LSUN)

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.split: FID against train and validation statistics
datasets.preprocessing: cropped and resized the same way as BigGAN; 32x32 base uses random left-right flips

models.name: ImageNet 32->64 SR
models.architecture: U-Net, class-conditional SR, amortized over s

training.objective: simple loss ||eps - eps_theta||^2 or hybrid loss Lsimple + lambda*Lvb (learned variances, 32 and 64 models); SR models trained with s~U({1..T}) conditioning noise level
training.hardware: 256 TPU-v3 cores (32x32, 32->64); 128 TPU-v3 cores (64->128, 64->256); 64 TPU-v3 cores (LSUN)

other.timesteps: 4000 cosine hybrid loss learned variances (32, 32->64); 2000 linear simple loss continuous noise conditioning (64->128, 64->256); LSUN simple loss continuous noise conditioning, cosine
other.conditioning_aug: Gaussian blur filter k=(3,3), sigma sampled from fixed range, applied to 50% of training examples, none at inference; best sigma~U(0.4,0.6)
other.batch_256_to_1024: increasing SR batch size from 256 to 1024 improved FID
other.early_stopping: model selection and early stopping on FID over 10k samples
other.non_cascaded_baseline: reimplemented Improved DDPM 4000-step 64x64 with dropout, trained longer, plus restart from noise to 2000 timestep point

inference.decoding: ancestral sampling; 4000 steps for 32 and 64 models; 100 steps for 128 and 256 SR (noise schedule tuned post-training); LSUN 256 steps
inference.samples: 50k samples for reported FID and IS (IS mean and std over 10 splits); 10k samples for model selection

parameters.inference_steps_256: 100 used; FID marginally worse at 4 steps, no gain 100->1000 (Fig 10)

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance on 50k samples vs train set stats (and validation stats)

metrics.name: IS
metrics.definition: Inception score, 50k samples, mean and std over 10 splits

metrics.name: CAS
metrics.definition: Classification Accuracy Score (Ravuri and Vinyals 2019): classifier trained on generated samples, tested on real validation images

eval.protocol: single run per config; no seeds or significance tests stated

availability.data: project page https://cascaded-diffusion.github.io/ (figures and supplementary only)

limits: ADM with classifier guidance outperforms CDM in FID and IS (authors concede)
Avoiding classifier guidance requires thousands of timesteps in low-res models (4000 vs ADM hundreds)
GANs beat CDM on Inception score when truncation is tuned for IS (BigGAN-deep max IS 253/317)
LOGAN 3.36 beats CDM 3.52 FID at 128x128 per Table 1a
Single runs, no seeds; training set FID used for selection (validation FID also reported)
Gaussian noise augmentation gave negative results at 128 and 256 upsampling, so blur is used there
Authors note possible malicious uses of image generation

terms.definition: data augmentation applied to the low resolution conditioning input of each super-resolution model
truncating the low resolution reverse process to stop at timestep s > 0 and conditioning on z_s
sample z0 with the full reverse process, then corrupt with the forward process to z'_s
